back: See and edit records = model-driven app. Something happens on change = flow or business rule. Ask in natural language = agent. Always equals a derived value = a column type. Keyword: pick the tool from the sentence.
Evaluate the agents Microsoft already ships before building one in Copilot Studio. Custom is warranted only when nothing shipped covers the task. Keyword: buy before build.
Configuration, then Power Fx, then plug-in or custom connector, then pro-code. Each rung up costs lifecycle and support. Keyword: lowest rung that works.
Every licensed user can create in it and it cannot be governed like a real environment. Never host a production business solution there. Keyword: default is not production.
Developer = free, single user, build here. Sandbox = copy, test, resettable. Production = users and support commitments. Keyword: build, test, serve.

Unmanaged is the editable source and belongs only in development. Managed is the deployed artefact, is not editable in the target, and uninstalls cleanly. Keyword: unmanaged in dev, managed downstream.
The prefix is baked into every schema name the solution creates and cannot be changed later. Set it before you build anything. Keyword: prefix is permanent.

Connection references and environment variables hold per-environment connection and configuration outside the component, so one managed solution serves test and production. Keyword: externalise what differs.
User-or-team ownership enables row-level security; organisation ownership does not. It is set at table creation and cannot be switched afterwards. Keyword: choose ownership once.

front: Many-to-many that needs its own data
back: An intersect table holds no attributes. If the relationship needs a date, role, or quantity, model it as a table between two one-to-many relationships. Keyword: the relationship is an entity.
Restrict Delete blocks deleting a parent that still has children. Remove Link clears the child's lookup instead of deleting the child. Keyword: block or unhook.

front: What does a prompt column cost?
back: A model call each time it runs. It is generated, not recalculated on read, so it is wrong for anything exact, current-to-the-second, or auditable. Keyword: interpretive values only.
A user gets the union of every role held directly and through teams. There is no deny. To remove access, remove a role — adding one can only widen. Keyword: no deny, ever.

front: Hiding a column on a form is not security
back: The data is still returned by the API, still in exports, still in advanced find. Only column-level security with a column security profile actually hides it. Keyword: form hiding is cosmetic.
Assign security roles to different main forms rather than building two apps. A form with no roles assigned is available to everyone. Keyword: roles on forms.

front: Search returns nothing for an obvious term
back: The quick find view decides which columns are searchable. A missing column there looks exactly like missing data. Keyword: check quick find first.
A page described in natural language and generated as real, editable app content — a solution component that moves between environments. Keyword: first draft, not a black box.
Adding a table to an app only puts it in navigation. Data access comes from security roles, configured elsewhere. Keyword: navigation is not permission.

front: Three independent things a user needs
back: A licence, a security role granting table privileges, and the app shared with them. Check all three; the first cause you find may not be the only one. Keyword: licence, role, share.

front: Why does one chart show different numbers?
back: A chart is built on a view and inherits its filter, and it honours row-level security. Different users legitimately see different totals. Keyword: charts obey the view.
Dashboard answers 'what do I work on next'. Power BI answers analytical questions across volume or systems — embed it, do not rebuild it as charts. Keyword: operational vs analytical.

front: What delegation actually does when it fails
back: Nothing errors. The expression is evaluated over the first 500 rows (up to 2,000) and returns a confident wrong answer. Keyword: silent, not broken.

The standard performance mistake: every row over the network at launch, breaks past the delegation limit, and stale for the session. Bind galleries to the source instead. Keyword: do not preload the table.
Set = global variable. UpdateContext = one screen only. ClearCollect = an in-memory table. Keyword: global, screen, table.
A named formula in App.Formulas is a definition — evaluated when read and always current. A variable set at start is stale the moment its inputs change, invisibly. Keyword: define, do not assign.
IfError and IsError inspect a result, Errors returns data-source errors after Patch or SubmitForm, and App.OnError is the last resort. Keyword: a silent Patch failure is the enemy.
Every network call, formula evaluation, and data operation with timing, on a published app as well as in the studio. Keyword: evidence, not guesswork.

front: When is an agent better than the app?
back: When the task is a request — check status, raise a simple item, answer a question. Not when it needs a form, a precise layout, or bulk work on many rows. Keyword: requests, not forms.

front: Three settings on the Dataverse trigger
back: Change type, scope, and select columns. Scope decides whose rows count — a flow that works only for its author is scoped to User. Keyword: scope is why it fires for nobody else.

It updates the row that triggered it. Fix on the trigger — select columns plus a trigger condition — because testing inside the flow still consumes a run and still loops. Keyword: fix it before it runs.
Every user who runs the flow needs the premium licence, not just the maker. Choosing a connector is a licensing decision. Keyword: the runner pays.

front: Reaching a source inside the corporate network
back: The on-premises data gateway. A custom connector wraps an API that has no connector — different problem, different tool. Keyword: gateway for network, custom connector for API.

front: The cost of raising Apply to each concurrency
back: Order is no longer guaranteed and any variable accumulated inside the loop races. Faster, and quietly wrong if the loop assumed sequence. Keyword: concurrency breaks accumulation.
A scope of actions, then a second scope with Configure run after set to has failed, timed out, or is skipped. Without it the flow just stops. Keyword: run after is the catch block.

front: Start and wait vs Create an approval
back: Start and wait blocks the flow until a response arrives. Create an approval sends it and continues, picking the outcome up later. Keyword: block or carry on.
Typically a lookup that was blank on the triggering row. The action fails there — it does not approve by default. Keyword: blank approver fails, not passes.

front: First to respond vs everyone must approve
back: First to respond closes on the first reply. Everyone must approve waits for all of them. Keyword: quorum of one, or of all.

front: What a 429 means and what it does not
back: Throttling. Slow down — reduce concurrency, add delay, batch. A tight retry loop extends the throttling rather than clearing it. Keyword: retrying harder makes it worse.

front: Whose identity does a flow act as?
back: Whoever created the connection, not whoever triggered the flow. That is what a 401 or 403 in run history is telling you. Keyword: the connection owner acts.
Resubmit replays a failed run with its original trigger payload once the cause is fixed, so the shape being tested is the real one. Keyword: replay the real payload.
Maximum run duration and per-connection request limits cannot be raised by asking. Work that exceeds them needs a different design — child flow, queue, or batch. Keyword: redesign, do not request.

front: What adding knowledge to a prompt fixes
back: Confident, plausible, wrong answers about internal matters. Grounding draws the answer from your content and makes it traceable to a source. Keyword: ground it or it guesses.

front: Constrain the output shape in the prompt
back: Ask for JSON with named fields, or one of a fixed list. A downstream flow parsing free prose breaks the first time the model rephrases. Keyword: shape the output, not just the answer.

front: Why save a prompt as a component?
back: One prompt then serves an app, a flow, and a prompt column with the same declared inputs and output, instead of being rewritten three times. Keyword: author once, consume anywhere.

Prebuilt covers invoices, receipts, business cards, text recognition, key phrases, language, sentiment — use it if it matches. Custom only for document or category sets unique to you. Keyword: prebuilt first.

front: Where the surprise AI Builder bill comes from
back: Credits are consumed per call. A prompt inside an Apply to each over a thousand rows is a thousand calls. Aggregate the input and call once where the task allows. Keyword: the loop is the bill.
Form scope runs client-side in that form only. Table scope also runs server-side, so it applies to imports, API writes, and flows. Keyword: form-only validation validates nothing.

front: Does a business process flow enforce anything?
back: No. It guides and presents stages. Data can still be written out of order by other means. Keyword: guidance, not enforcement.

front: Why a rollup column shows stale totals
back: It is computed by a scheduled system job, hourly by default. It is eventually consistent by design and cannot be made real-time. Keyword: rollups run on a clock.
Calculated and formula evaluate on read and are always current; formula uses Power Fx and is the modern default. Rollup aggregates children on a schedule. Keyword: on read, or on a clock.
